sections.text:
Yunus, peace be upon him (who is nicknamed Dhul-Nun) is a noble prophet, sent by God to the people of the city of Nineveh in the land of Iraq, and their number was very large, exceeding one hundred thousand people.

The people of Nineveh worshiped idols, and corruption and injustice spread among them. Yunus called on them to unite God, abandon polytheism, and change their corrupt behavior, but they rejected him, opposed him, and mocked his call.

Yunus continued to call them day and night for a long time, warning them of the wrath of God, but they insisted on their disbelief and challenged him to bring them torment if he was sincere.

Yunus felt extremely angry and desperate about their faith, and he could no longer bear to remain among them, so he decided to leave them and leave Medina without waiting for permission and approval from God Almighty.

Before he left the city in anger, he warned them that God's punishment would befall them after three days if they did not repent.

Yunus boarded a ship with a group of travelers and merchants to get away from Nineveh as quickly as possible. At sea, a violent storm and strong waves arose that almost drowned the ship with all its passengers.

The travelers threw their luggage to lighten the load, but the storm intensified, and the sailors said: “There is a disobedient man among us. We must throw him into the sea so that the ship can survive!”

They drew lots to find out who they would meet, and Yunus' arrow came out! They were amazed because he seemed like a good man, so they repeated it three times and each time his name came out.

Yunus realized in his believing heart that this was a test from God and a punishment for leaving his people without permission, so he rose up and threw his body into the turbulent, turbulent sea.

At that moment, God commanded a huge whale to swallow Jonah, and inspired the whale not to break his bones or scratch his flesh, for he was not food but a prisoner in his stomach!
Yunus found himself trapped in three desolate darknesses: the darkness of the brutal night, the darkness of the deep sea floor, and the suffocating darkness of the whale’s belly.

Yunus became aware of his mistake and haste, and he prostrated himself in the belly of the whale, and began to repeat the greatest supplication in history with all brokenness and hope: “There is no god but You, Glory be to You. Indeed, I have been of the wrongdoers.”

He kept repeating this supplication with a humble and remorseful heart, asking for forgiveness. Then the angels heard his voice and recognized him, and said: O Lord, a weak, well-known voice from a strange land!
God answered his prayer with His grace and mercy, and commanded the whale to devour Jonah and bring him out safely on a barren, treeless beach.

Yunus's body was weak, sick, and delicate as a young bird's chick due to the acids of the whale's stomach and his absence from the sun.

God grew on him a tree of “pumpkin” (pumpkin) that shaded him with its broad, cool leaves and nourished him with its fruits, because it is a tree that flies do not approach, so they do not harm his sick body.

As for his people in Nineveh, when they saw the black clouds of torment gathering and approaching three days after Jonah’s departure, they realized his sincerity and felt extreme terror.

They all went out to the desert, men, women, children, and even their animals, crying and supplicating to God. They separated the mothers and their children to make the crying louder, asking God to pardon them and accept their repentance.

God accepted their repentance and lifted the torment from them in a rare historical moment that did not happen to any other people. God Almighty said: (Except the people of Yunus, when they believed, We removed from them the torment of disgrace).

When Yunus recovered, God commanded him to return to his people, so he returned to them to find that they had all believed and were certain in the One and Only God. He rejoiced in them and lived with them teaching them their religion until God took his death.
